title: Classes and objects: what exists at runtime

videos.script: Every program so far has been one class with one method in it. This lesson writes a class that is not a program at all. It describes a thing. {{class}} A book, with an ISBN, a title and a year. Four lines. Nothing runs when it compiles. {{new}} Then the word new, which makes one. And then another. Two books from one class, each with its own title. {{references}} The variable you hold is not the book. It is the way to the book. Copy the variable, and you have two ways to one book. Set it to null, and you have none, and Java tells you so, by name. {{heap}} Last, the books themselves. A thousand of them, counted inside a running JVM. Twenty-four bytes each. By the end you can say what a class is, what an object is, and where each one lives while the program runs.
